contexts.text: That to which he is compelled is not his...
That they were not his. Signified.
That whatever man does from freedom... appears to him as his.
(Necessity of) the appearance that it is his.
So far as man acknowledges this, the Lord grants that good may appear to man as his...
Good and truth appear to man as from himself and as his, just as if they were his; there is no difference...
It is this will of the Lord which makes what a man thinks, speaks, wills, and does, appear in him as his.
Nor would anything appear to man as his.
These faculties... are not appropriated to man as his; for what is Divine cannot be appropriated to man as his; but it can be adjoined to him, and thereby appear as if it were his...
He who confirms... the appearance, that wisdom and prudence are... in man as his...
These things cannot be united to the recipient so as to be his...
